cases.question: How do I make Le Tourin garlic soup?

response.answer: Le Tourin is a garlic soup from the village of Le Fleix in Dordogne, serving 2 and taking 30 minutes in total. To make it: 1. In a frying pan, brown the chopped garlic in the olive oil. 2. Add the flour, mix well, then cook for a few minutes to remove the floury taste. 3. Gradually stir in the water and cook for 10 minutes. 4. Beat the egg white in a small bowl, gradually whisk in a ladleful of the soup to temper it, then stir the mixture back into the soup pot. 5. Combine the egg yolk, pepper and vinegar in a small bowl, then gradually temper the yolks with a ladleful of soup. 6. Remove the soup from the heat, stir in the egg yolk mixture and season to taste with salt. 7. Place thin slices of bread in each soup bowl, pour the soup on top and serve hot. A variant noted on the page uses an equal mixture of chopped onions and garlic instead of garlic alone. The ingredient list comes from the source page and may be incomplete.

cases.question: What's the method for pasta carbonara?

response.answer: The first recipe, Spaghetti alla Carbonara, is made as follows. Dice the guanciale or pancetta into 2.5 cm pieces. Bring a big pot of water to a boil and add salt when it begins to simmer. Cook the spaghetti until al dente, drain it, and reserve 1 cup of the water. While the spaghetti cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the pancetta and cook for about 10 minutes over a low flame until most of its fat has rendered but it is still chewy and barely browned. In a bowl, slowly whisk about ½ cup of the pasta water into the egg yolks, add the grated cheese and mix thoroughly with a fork. Strain the spaghetti and transfer it immediately to the skillet with the pancetta, toss and turn off the heat. Add the egg and cheese mixture while stirring in the remaining pasta water to thin the sauce and create an emulsion. Add the pepper and toss to coat the pasta. A second recipe, Carbonara Pasta, is a variant that uses no olive oil in the pan, fries cubed pancetta in a dry pan, cools it, and mixes it with egg yolks, lemon zest, thyme and onion-free seasoning instead of a pasta-water emulsion. The ingredient lists come from the source pages and may be incomplete.

cases.question: What can I cook with garbanzo beans?

response.answer: You can make Qabuli (Central Asian Rice Pilaf), which uses 500 g of dry chickpeas, the garbanzo bean's other name, along with rice, onions, tomato paste, spices, cilantro and green chiles. The page does not state a total cooking time or number of servings. The ingredient list comes from the source page and may be incomplete. Ingredients: 500 g dry chickpeas, salt, red pepper, ½ tsp ginger garlic paste, 1 kg rice, shortening, 3 onions chopped, chile powder, tomato paste, ¼ tsp turmeric powder, ½ cup chopped cilantro, 4–5 green chiles cut in half. Steps: 1. Soak the chickpeas for half an hour. 2. Boil the chickpeas with salt, red pepper, and ginger garlic paste until no water remains. 3. If water remains, continue cooking until mostly absorbed. 4. Bring the rice to a full boil, reduce heat to a minimum and cover, cook 8–10 minutes, then turn off the heat and rest for a similar time. 5. Heat shortening in a pan, fry the onions until light brown, then add tomato paste, salt, red chile powder and turmeric powder. 6. Arrange the fried onion mixture, boiled chickpeas and rice in a large serving dish pot. 7. Garnish with chopped cilantro and green chillies and serve hot.

Place the rice in the upper part of a double boiler with 3 cups (750 ml) half and half, 1 cup (225 g) granulated sugar, 1 cinnamon stick and 1 piece of lemon peel. Bring to a boil over direct heat, then place over simmering water in the double boiler and cook for 45 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon peel, pour the mixture into a 2-quart (1.9 L) casserole, allow it to cool, and sprinkle with ground cinnamon.
